PAGE TITLE:
Civil Monetary Penalty Adjustment for Inflation

PHOTOS:
- Photo of a NASA astronaut and Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman participating in training Jan. 23 in the Neutral Buoyancy Lab at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston.
  - Photo caption: NASA astronaut and Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman participates in training Jan. 23 in the Neutral Buoyancy Lab at the agency's Johnson Space Center in Houston.
  - Photo credit: PHOTO CREDIT - NASA Johnson Space Center
- Photo in the "Did You Know?" section: The Cygnus space freighter fires its engine to raise the station's orbital altitude.
  - Photo caption: The Cygnus space freighter fires its engine to raise the station's orbital altitude. This long-duration photograph taken with a station camera uses increased sensitivity and shows the Northrop Grumman Cygnus space freighter firing its engine to raise the International Space Station's orbital altitude. The reboosts counteract atmospheric drag and prepare for the space station upcoming spacecraft activities. The orbital outpost was soaring 263 miles above the Indian Ocean with a field of star trails above and the Aurora Australis below.
  - Photo credit: PHOTO CREDIT - NASA Johnson

KEY FACTS:
- The Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015 (P.L. 114-74) requires agencies to make annual inflation adjustments to civil monetary penalties and report on these adjustments in their AFR.
- Penalty updates are located in the Federal Register Volume 89, No. 56 at govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-03-21/pdf/2024-05999.pdf.
- The orbital outpost was soaring 263 miles above the Indian Ocean.
